From: Elena Soto <elena.soto@atlasai.com>
To: priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Launch checklist — cost/perf concerns

Hi Priyom —

Thanks for the quick demo last week. We are on track for our feature launch in mid-Jan, but the product team flagged token cost as the single biggest gating item. I attached a 7-day sample of traffic (prod_usage_sample.csv) and our current inference diagram (architecture_diagram.png). A few asks up front:

- We need a clear, prioritized set of tuning levers we can run during the next two sprints (batching, cache configs, quant profiles, routing).
- We need a canary rollout plan that keeps p95 latency < 350ms for our primary route while reducing per-token cost by ~20%.
- We will need Redwood engineers to access telemetry (read-only) and a short workshop with your CS/solutions team next week.

We are sensitive to output quality: aggressive quantization has caused hallucination risk in other vendors, so we want a safe baseline and a staged approach.

Thanks — I can host the kickoff if that helps.

--
Elena Soto
Head of Product, Atlas AI

Elena — thanks for the signal and the attachments. Got them and skimmed the sample. Happy to run a focused workshop and leave you with an actionable mini-playbook plus a canary schedule. Proposed next steps: 

1) 60-minute kickoff (Monica + Marcus + me) to align on success metrics (cost delta, latency SLOs, quality guardrails) — propose Thursday 12/4 at 10am PT.
2) Workshop (90m) with devs where we:
   - map real request distributions to static/dynamic batching targets
   - set up prefix/KV cache with TTL guidance for your short-lived contexts
   - evaluate 3 quant profiles on a holdout prompt set (Q8_HYBRID, Q4_SAFE, FP16 baseline)
   - draft routing policy: primary low-latency route (FP16/opt) + cost-fallback (Q8_HYBRID) with automatic rollback on quality regressions
3) 2-week canary: start with 5% traffic -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% with automated evals and latency/cost dashboards.

I added Monica (CS lead) and Marcus (solutions eng) to help run the workshop and own the MAP deliverable. To be sure we hit your constraints we will need read-only telemetry access (requesting a short-lived API key/role) and a sample prompt set for quality checks.

Happy to adjust timing.

Thanks,
Priyom

Thanks all — quick note on what we'll bring to the workshop and the short-term tuning defaults we typically try at this stage: 

- Workshop deliverables: mutual action plan PDF, step-by-step runbook for batching/cache, a set of eval prompts + pass/fail criteria, and a recommended canary script for Redwood Console.
- Default starting levers (we tune from here):
  * batching: target dynamic batch sizes between 8-32 for interactive latency profiles; 32-128 for async bulk jobs. Start with upper bound 16 for your traffic mix.
  * caching: prefix-based KV cache (TTL 30s-2m) for session-heavy flows; add an LRU short-term response cache for exact-match completions.
  * quant profiles: run FP16 baseline, then Q8_HYBRID for lowest win/quality tradeoff; Q4_SAFE only in isolated evals (we do not recommend global Q4 for customer-facing routing until regressions are understood).
  * routing: set a cost-tier fallback route and an automatic rollback on eval-drop > 2% or p95 latency > 350ms.

Required from Atlas before the workshop: read-only telemetry role + a 200-500 prompt eval set (we can redact PII). If you prefer, we can run the evals on a synthetic subset we assemble from the sample CSV.

Link to proposed MAP and HubSpot record: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/atlasai (see tasks we created).

See you on the call.

—Monica
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: MAP_Atlas_Team_v1.pdf (updated)]

Monica — appreciate the clear defaults. A couple of clarifications:

- We will provision a read-only service principal and I assigned infra@atlasai.com to share the key with your team. Expected to be ready by Wednesday 12/9.
- For evals: we'll push a 300-prompt holdout set (no PII) and start with Q8_HYBRID vs FP16. Our product team is wary of Q4 because some of our generative completion prompts are highly factual and short-context (we saw degradation with other vendors).
- Canary cadence: for our users the p95 SLA is strict during business hours; can we scope the canary to off-peak windows (10pm-4am PT) by default? That will give us quieter telemetry to assess cost/quality.

If that works I'll confirm the workshop time (Thu 12/10 10am PT) and send attendees.

Elena — confirmed for Thu 12/10 10am PT, invite sent. A few tactical items I wanted to capture before the workshop so we can move fast: 

1) Evaluation plan (automated): run A/B on 300 prompt holdout set comparing FP16 vs Q8_HYBRID. Metrics: exact-match rate (when applicable), ROUGE-L / semantic similarity, mean token cost, 50/95/99 latency. Pass criteria = no >2% drop in quality metrics and p95 latency <= 350ms on canary windows.

2) Canary script (automated steps):
   - Step 0: Baseline: capture 24h baseline traffic for metrics.
   - Step 1: 5% traffic -> run evals every 2h -> if pass, increase to 25%.
   - Step 2: 25% -> 50% (after two passing windows).
   - Step 3: 100% + monitor for 24h.
   - Auto-rollback triggers: eval drop > 2% OR p95 > 350ms OR error rate increase > 0.5%.

3) Recommended starting model profiles (internal names):
   - redwood/falcon-7b-fp16: baseline
   - redwood/falcon-7b-q8hybrid: cost-optimized fallback
   - redwood/falcon-7b-q4safe: evaluation-only (reserved)

4) Dashboards/alerts: we'll create a per-route dashboard and a Canary run card in Redwood Console; link will be shared in the MAP doc.

I'll prep a short eval-run (HB-7321) and share results in the workshop. Looking forward to the call.

—Marcus
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
